title: Rast wins the 500th DTM race as Audi takes the manufacturers’ title
dek: René Rast won DTM Race 2 at the Lausitzring by 5.187 seconds from Nico Müller, who dropped to tenth on the opening lap, and Audi took the first five places and the manufacturers’ title.

chapters.title: Saturday’s upset, and a milestone race to come
text: Saturday had gone to Nico Müller. He won Race 1 from Robin Frijns and Mike Rockenfeller for an Audi one-two-three after René Rast, who had started from pole, lost power and retired from the lead. Rast stayed on 209 points and Müller closed to 195, just 14 behind, while Marco Wittmann was fourth on the road and 50 points off the lead.

Sunday’s race was the 500th in the history of the DTM, which began in 1984. Track temperatures on Sunday reached about 40 degrees Celsius, which put the Hankook tyres and the pit-stop strategies under pressure. Audi, with the top three places on Saturday, was close to the manufacturers’ title.

chapters.title: Green takes pole as the title rivals fail to improve
text: Jamie Green went top on the first runs and set the benchmark of 1m35.397s, his first pole since the Red Bull Ring in September 2017 and the 14th of his DTM career. Müller and Rast, who had been second and third behind him after the first runs, could not find any improvement in the final minutes.

That opened the door for Jonathan Aberdein. The WRT rookie set three personal-best sectors to jump from a provisional ninth to second on 1m35.498s, 0.101 seconds behind Green, his third front-row start of the season. Müller was third, 0.151 seconds off, with Rast fourth, 0.212 seconds back, so the title rivals shared the second row. Frijns completed an all-Audi top five.

Wittmann was sixth, 0.250 seconds off, and said BMW saw no way to match the Audis at that point. Duval was seventh and Fittipaldi eighth. Glock was the second BMW in ninth, ahead of Rockenfeller, followed by Sheldon van der Linde, Eriksson and Spengler. Di Resta was the best Aston Martin in 14th, ahead of Dennis, Habsburg and Juncadella. Eng started from the back of the grid.

chapters.title: Müller’s start goes wrong, Rast takes the lead on lap four
text: Müller made a poor start from third and had dropped to 11th by the first corner, finishing lap one tenth. Aberdein was also slow away from the front row. Rast, on the outside of row two, went straight to second, and Green kept the lead. Wittmann also lost two places at the start, which he put down to wheelspin.

Rast followed Green closely and passed him on the run to the Turn 1 right-hander on lap four, with little resistance from the pole-sitter, who said afterwards that helping his team-mate to the title was part of his job. Rast then pulled clear. Eng, starting last, climbed to 11th within a few laps. Behind them, Dennis stopped within the first laps, and Habsburg, who made contact with Glock at Turn 1, was out soon after.

chapters.title: Müller’s undercut, a slow stop for Green and BMW’s second stops
text: Spengler opened the mandatory stops on lap seven. Müller, stuck in ninth behind Wittmann, followed on lap eight in an undercut attempt, together with Rockenfeller, and the Abt crew changed his tyres in 7.2 seconds. Rockenfeller held him up for several laps, but Müller passed him on lap 12 to head the pack behind Rast, who stopped for his own tyres on the same lap.

Frijns, who stopped with Rast, was passed in turn by several Audi team-mates on his cold tyres. Rast rejoined with a comfortable gap and later stretched it to more than seven seconds. Green, who had led before his stop, came in on lap 17 and was held up by a slow stop of 8.7 seconds that dropped him behind the group chasing Rast. Wittmann stopped on the same lap in 6.5 seconds. In the heat, the BMW drivers struggled with their tyres in the closing stages, and several of them came in for a second stop. Juncadella held some of them back in the Aston Martin.

chapters.title: Rast wins by 5.2 seconds ahead of Müller and Rockenfeller
text: Rast took the flag after 34 laps in 56m59.382s, 5.187 seconds ahead of Müller, who had recovered to second. Rockenfeller was third, 8.953 seconds off, as he had been on Saturday, and defended the place against Green, whose fresher tyres brought him to within 0.665 seconds at the line in fourth. Frijns was fifth at 11.341 seconds, which gave Audi the top five places. Wittmann, sixth, was the best BMW.

Aberdein, Duval and Fittipaldi were seventh, eighth and ninth, so all eight Audis finished in the top nine. Eng recovered from last to 10th and set the fastest lap, a 1m37.897s on lap 10. Van der Linde was 11th and Juncadella 12th, the only Aston Martin to finish. Eriksson was 13th, Spengler 14th and Glock 15th, nine laps down. Di Resta retired after being pushed off the track by Spengler, and with Habsburg and Dennis already out, Juncadella was the only R-Motorsport driver to see the flag.

chapters.title: Rast extends his lead to 20 points and Audi seals the manufacturers’ title
text: Rast called the start the key to his race and said his pace afterwards had been gigantic. He admitted that after nearly half an hour on one set of tyres he heard every noise from the car, and that he had hoped nothing would go wrong, and he dedicated the win to the mechanics who had worked on the car late into the night after Saturday. The only tricky moment was a patch of dirt on the track, where his front-left wheel briefly came to a standstill. Asked about the title, he said he would not claim it, but that it would be important to win it. Müller said he had had a small clutch problem all weekend, thought he could survive with it and then made a mistake at the start, which left him with a lucky escape. Rockenfeller said he had worried in the closing laps that Green, on fresher tyres, would catch him, but that his tyres lasted to the flag. Green said it was his job to help Rast.

The championship moved Rast’s way. He now led Müller by 20 points, 234 to 214, with Wittmann third on 167, 67 behind. Four races remained, and Hankook’s motorsport director said the Nürburgring and the Hockenheim finale promised exciting racing, with Müller still well placed.

Audi had its first title of the year. With the top five places on Sunday, adding to Saturday’s top three, it could no longer be caught in the manufacturers’ classification with two weekends and four races still to run. The BMW drivers had no answer: Wittmann said the Audis had too much, while the championship was running away. Audi’s motorsport chief Dieter Gass praised the car and the team for sealing the title so early in the season.
It was a difficult day for Aston Martin, with three of its four cars out. The DTM now moves on to the Nürburgring on 14–15 September, before the finale at Hockenheim in October.

facts.v: Rast won the 500th race in DTM history, 5.187 seconds clear of Müller, to take his fifth win of the season.
